title: Separate network-attachment module and rotate GPU instance roles for private deploys
author: Priya Menon
description: Context: Private deployments need a clearer separation between the network attachment lifecycle and GPU node class IAM identity material. Current modules embed ENI/subnet attachments with nodepool lifecycle which makes cross-account routing and ephemeral subnet workflows brittle. This PR extracts a dedicated modules/network-attachment, introduces an explicit gpu-instance-roles module with rotation helpers, and provides a migration plan for existing tfstate prefixes. Motivation: decoupling allows: 1) independent rollout of subnet attachments and nodeclass updates; 2) safer IAM role rotation for GPU instances (workload-identity-friendly) without touching nodepool provisioning; 3) simpler rollbacks for network changes. Design: - modules/network-attachment: owns VPC attachment resources, route table associations, and a small controller-configmap example for the installer to watch attachment state. It exposes outputs for attachment ids and recommended lifecycle hooks. - modules/gpu-instance-roles: defines instance profile, IAM role with least-privilege policies for GPU nodeclasses, optional OIDC trust binding, and an id_rotation submodule (script + TF null_resource) that coordinates key rotation using a locked tfstate object. - state migration helper: a terraform-migrate.sh script and brief instructions to move network attachment state to a new tfstate prefix (non-destructive plan-first workflow). - examples/private-deploy: updated example showing how to wire the new modules and an annotation-based rollout pattern for the installer. Testing and validation: - terraform validate/plan on the new modules with a small mock VPC. - end-to-end deploy to a staging VPC in our CI tenant with ephemeral subnet lifecycles. - IAM role rotation exercised in a dry-run mode before final rotation. Rollout notes: - Step 1: Deploy modules/network-attachment into a new state prefix using terraform-migrate.sh plan-only flag to ensure no surprise deletions. - Step 2: Deploy modules/gpu-instance-roles in parallel (they do not own the same resources) and run the id_rotation in dry-run. - Step 3: Once validated, trigger the rotation plan and coordinate with the installer to drain and restart a small percentage of GPU nodes. Rollback plan: revert to previous tfstate backups made by terraform-migrate.sh and use the installer annotation to pin older nodeclass versions. Security considerations: IAM policies were tightened compared to prior roles (removed broad iam:PassRole and limited trust principals with conditions). The rotation helper requires short-lived credentials and logs to a customer-managed CloudAudit log path. Migration caveats: for on-prem customers with air-gapped environments, the id_rotation uses a local keyfile path fallback and will not attempt remote KMS calls; documentation enumerates manual steps. Related work items: ENG-1387 (network module review), ENG-1429 (gpu identity rotation RFC). Checklist: - [x] module code and unit tests - [x] terraform validate/plan - [x] e2e staging deploy - [x] docs and upgrade notes - [x] security review

review_comments: Ethan Brooks: Why extract network attachments separately? Concern about ordering between attachment and nodepool applies. Can we make the attachment resource create-before-destroy?
Priya Menon: Addressed by adding lifecycle create_before_destroy on associations and documented the required ordering in the upgrade notes.
Lin Zhao: IAM policy looks permissive for KMS usage during rotation — can we restrict to KMS key ARNs and add condition on encryption-context?
Priya Menon: Scoped the KMS permissions and added a rotation mode for air-gapped customers that uses local keyfiles; documented the security tradeoffs.
Marco D'Souza: CI plan failed first run due to missing provider pin; re-ran and passed. Approving the change.
merge_outcome: merged after CI rerun and reviewer approvals
release_notes: Decouple network attachment lifecycle from nodepool provisioning for private deployments.
Introduce gpu-instance-roles module with rotation helper and tighter IAM policies.
Add terraform-migrate.sh helper to move attachment state to a new prefix safely.
No automatic changes to existing nodepools; follow upgrade guide to migrate state and perform rotation.
notes_for_ops: Operators must run terraform-migrate.sh plan-only first and ensure tfstate backups are taken. For customers using KMS, update the allowed KMS key ARNs in the new module config before rotation. On-prem installs should follow the air-gap rotation flow documented in docs/upgrade-guides/2026-02-network-attachment-and-role-rotation.md.
testing_steps: 1) terraform init && terraform validate on modules/network-attachment and modules/gpu-instance-roles; 2) run terraform-migrate.sh --dry-run against staging state backend; 3) apply network-attachment, then apply gpu-instance-roles in staging; 4) run id_rotation in dry-run; 5) coordinate small node drain and rotate in production.
changelog_summary: Refactors: moved network attachment into dedicated module; added dedicated GPU instance IAM roles with rotation tooling; added migration helper script and docs.
customer_impact: Low by default. Migration is opt-in. If operators follow the documented plan, there should be no downtime. Rotation requires sequential node restarts which are coordinated and gradual.
